en.name: Clement I
en.summary: The fourth Bishop of Rome and author of the Epistle to the Corinthians, one of the earliest and most important Christian documents outside the New Testament.
en.body: Clement I is the earliest post-apostolic pope for whom a genuine surviving writing exists: his Epistle to the Corinthians, sent to settle a leadership dispute in the Corinthian church, is among the oldest Christian texts outside the New Testament and was read aloud in some churches' liturgies for generations afterward. It shows a Roman church already asserting a measure of authority over disputes in other Christian communities. Later tradition, of uncertain reliability, holds he was exiled and martyred by drowning near the Crimea.
